1.explanation: Prism’s C++ language support is built on top of the “clike” grammar defined in prism-clike.js (and its minified version). The C++-specific rules in prism-cpp.js (and its minified version) extend that grammar. The failure to highlight inherited class names (‘QMainWindow’) and scoped class members (‘MainWindow::…’) stems from how classes and identifiers are tokenized in those two files. To fix the issue, you’ll need to adjust the class-name patterns in prism-clike.js (so base classes after the colon are captured) and/or extend them in prism-cpp.js (so scoped identifiers following `ClassName::` are recognized).
1.bug_scenario: In the provided screenshots and code snippet, PrismJS correctly highlights the first class name “MainWindow” after the ‘class’ keyword, but it fails to highlight: 1) the base class identifier ‘QMainWindow’ in the inheritance list, and 2) the class name ‘MainWindow’ in the member definition after the scope operator (`MainWindow::changeWindowTitle`). Prism’s C++ grammar doesn’t recognize identifiers in those contexts as class names, whereas GitHub’s highlighter does.

2.explanation: Prism’s C++ support is built on top of the “clike” language definition (in prism-clike.js). The clike grammar provides general rules for class names and identifiers, but the C++ extension in prism-cpp.js does not add patterns for base‐class names in inheritance clauses nor for qualified class names in method definitions. To fix the missing highlights, the class-name pattern in prism-cpp.js needs to be extended (or overridden) to recognize identifiers following a colon in a class declaration and the qualifier before “::” in member definitions. Both the non‐minified and minified versions of prism-clike.js and prism-cpp.js must be updated so that C++ class names in these contexts are correctly tokenized and styled.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting C++ code with PrismJS both the name of a base class in an inheritance clause (for example, "QMainWindow" in "class MainWindow : public QMainWindow") and a qualified identifier in a method definition (for example, "MainWindow" in "void MainWindow::changeWindowTitle()") are not being recognized and styled as class names. GitHub’s highlighter correctly highlights those identifiers, but Prism’s existing CPP grammar in prism-cpp.js (which extends the prism-clike grammar) fails to handle these cases.
